goal: Implement the framework-neutral solver training validation layer that the failed v1 test expected. Combine masked soft-policy cross-entropy and legal-action top-1 accuracy into SolverTrainingMetrics, export the existing training contracts through poker.solver, and record the next concrete boundary gap.

operations.old: The next solver step should reconcile these small training-boundary modules into one coherent public solver API and define masked soft-policy loss/metric semantics against legal-action masks before any concrete trainer or model implementation. Because these are solver-local contracts rather than production poker-engine behavior, focused solver tests are sufficient until a cross-subsystem training integration is introduced.
operations.new: The solver training boundary now also has a framework-neutral validation layer: `evaluate_solver_predictions()` combines the existing masked soft-policy cross-entropy objective with deterministic legal-action top-1 accuracy and returns `SolverTrainingMetrics`. The training contracts are exported through `poker.solver` so future consumers do not need to import internal module paths. No tensor backend, model, optimizer or Arena integration is introduced. The next solver step should make legal-action masks first-class data in `SolverTrainingBatch` and connect `SolverTrainingInput` -> batch -> validation end-to-end, removing the remaining mismatch where batches currently carry observations/probabilities but not masks. This remains solver-local, so focused validation is sufficient until a concrete trainer or cross-subsystem integration is added.
